#Bird of the Day: Long-billed Curlew (LBCU)
Also known as the “sicklebird” for obvious reasons, the LBCU is a type of sandpiper-- the largest of that family regularly seen in North America. Although the plumage of both adults looks the same, they do display sexual dimorphism in that females are

larger and generally have longer bills than the males. That long bill, typically 7-9” (but appearing even longer to me), is used to probe the mud and sand for small crabs and other invertebrates. Another nickname for the LBCU is the “candlestick #bird” and over a hundred years ago there was a large

flock residing within San Francisco Bay. 🪶 The name Candlestick Point was given to the flat area of jutting out into the water (now reclaimed as Candlestick Point State Recreation Area after decades of being used as a dumpsite) and subsequently the outdoor sports stadium Candlestick Park

began construction in the 1950s. But by that time, the LBCU were largely gone from the area, moving to less urban areas. Overall, world populations of this #bird are stable and healthy. They seem able to adapt and relocate to new feeding and nesting grounds when disturbed.
